student_answers.answer_text: Atomicity means the transaction is all-or-nothing: either all changes commit or the DBMS rolls everything back on failure. Consistency means after commit the database still satisfies its integrity constraints — it moves from one valid state to another. Isolation means concurrent transactions do not interfere; each behaves as if it ran alone (or at least does not see dirty intermediate states). Durability means once committed, the results survive a crash because they are written to stable storage / the log.

A = all operations succeed or none (rollback). C = constraints/rules still hold after the transaction. I = transactions appear not to step on each other while running together. D = committed updates are permanent even after power loss.
